en:Este es un pollo de supermercado. Tie: This is a supermarket chicken. You have to buy the best quality. Because this Hainanese chicken rice dish is all about the pure flavor of chicken, you really want to go with organic. It's worth it for the palate.
en:Cómo darle a tu pollo un tratamiento: How to give your chicken a spa treatment. Start with a small handful of coarse salt. Regular table salt is too fine to use for exfoliation. Sea salt is very expensive. Just use coarse salt. Even if you don't have that loose skin on your chicken, that doesn't mean you don't need to exfoliate.
en:Sazone el interior y el exterior del: Season the inside and outside of the chicken with salt and stuff the bird with ginger and scallions. Remember, not only are you seasoning the chicken, but the water turns into broth, so be generous with the salt.

en:Pon a hervir a ese bebé y luego inmed: Bring that baby to a boil and then immediately lower the heat to keep it simmering. You will start to see a white, floating foam, which is actually denatured protein. I have a handy skimmer. If you don't have a skimmer, buy one, it's only $100! The foam clouds the soup (and just doesn't taste good), so it's best to remove it.
en:Después de hervir a fuego lento (lo s: After simmering (long enough for small bubbles to come to the surface) and your chicken reaches the correct temperature (take the temperature of the chicken at the thickest part of the thigh that doesn't touch the bone, it should read 80 degrees). This is done!
en:Prepare un baño de hielo e inmediatam: Prepare an ice bath and immediately lift the chicken from the pot with 2 large slotted spoons or 2 large thick spatulas.
en:Consejo: No intente agarrar las patas: Tip: Do not try to grab the chicken legs to remove the chicken. You'll end up tearing the skin and maybe even ripping the drumsticks off the chicken...which results in you standing there holding two thighs, while the rest of the chicken falls back into the boiling broth...which then splatters all over your arms and face. Speaking from experience, of course. Oh, and don't even THINK about pouring that clean, delicious broth down the sink. We will use it to cook the rice, prepare the sauce and drink as soup! So, remember, gently lift the chicken from underneath and try not to disturb its delicate (and exfoliated!) skin. My pot of ice water wasn't big enough, but it worked, I just turned the chicken a few times to make sure both sides were cold. Immersion in an ice bath stops the cooking process immediately AND firms the skin, making it elastic and firm. The quality of the chicken skin is important in this dish! It's all about the texture of the skin. Part 2: Hainanese Chicken Rice Soup Look here? That's your soup! Taste and season with salt, if necessary. Part 3: Cooking Hainanese Rice Clean Rice After soaking, drain as much water as possible. Sauté Garlic and Ginger Take a pot and sauté the garlic and ginger and chopped chicken fat. Mmmm...can you smell that? Add drained rice to pot. Fry the rice grains for a minute...this gives the rice so much flavor! I like to add a little salt to the rice. Cook rice with chicken broth. Remember that broth? Well, pour 2 cups of this into the pot. Normally when I cook rice, I would go with a ratio of 1 cup rice: 1.25 cups water/broth. But since we've already soaked the rice and the rice has absorbed some of the water, I'm going with 1:1. Bring the rice to a boil, then immediately lower the heat, cover tightly, and cook for 15 minutes. Remove from heat and let sit (still covered! Don't open!) for 5-10 more minutes. Made. TIP: Oh, if you have a rice cooker, even better! Sauté the ginger and garlic and chicken fat in a small pot on the stove (some rice cookers have a sauté function). Add rice, sauté for a minute. Then, pour everything into the rice cooker, including the broth, and start cooking. Perfect rice: fluffy and fluffy. Part 4: Ginger Garlic Chili Sauce for Hainanese Chicken Rice Chili Sauce If you are a fan of Sriracha chili sauce, this will knock your socks off. Jess puts sriracha, lime, sugar, salt, a couple tablespoons of that delicious chicken broth, garlic and ginger in a blender and wheeeeeee: Ginger Garlic Sauce I don't have a photo of ginger garlic sauce, but it is often served with Hainanese chicken. The recipe is simple: Fresh ginger + finely chopped garlic with a little salt and a splash of vinegar. The best way to chop ginger is to grate the peeled ginger with a microplane. The (or grater) will create superfine ginger, leaving the fibrous parts behind. Garlic is best minced with a garlic press or garlic chopper and mix everything. Serve the chicken boneless and chopped. Enjoy!!
en:Yo uso arroz jazmín o arroz de grano: I use jasmine rice or long grain rice. To feed six people, I am using 2 cups of uncooked rice. Place the rice in a large container and fill with water. Use your hands to move the rice around. This helps remove excess starch and other rice additives, such as powder. Carefully tilt the bowl to drain the water, using your hands to keep the rice in the bowl. Repeat 3 more times. The water will never be "clear", but it will be less cloudy. Fill the container again with fresh water and let the rice soak in water for 10 minutes.

pt:Este es un pollo de supermercado. Tie: Esta é uma galinha de supermercado. Você tem que comprar a melhor qualidade. Como este prato de arroz com frango Hainanese tem tudo a ver com o sabor puro do frango, você realmente quer optar pelo orgânico. Vale a pena pelo paladar.
pt:Cómo darle a tu pollo un tratamiento: Como dar um tratamento de spa ao seu frango. Comece com um pequeno punhado de sal grosso. O sal de cozinha comum é muito fino para ser usado na esfoliação. O sal marinho é muito caro. Basta usar sal grosso. Mesmo que você não tenha aquela pele solta no frango, isso não significa que não precise esfoliar.
pt:Sazone el interior y el exterior del: Tempere o interior e o exterior do frango com sal e recheie o pássaro com gengibre e cebolinha. Lembre-se, você não só tempera o frango, mas a água vira caldo, então seja generoso com o sal.

pt:Yo uso arroz jazmín o arroz de grano: Eu uso arroz jasmim ou arroz de grão longo. Para alimentar seis pessoas, estou usando 2 xícaras de arroz cru. Coloque o arroz em um recipiente grande e encha com água. Use as mãos para mover o arroz. Isso ajuda a remover o excesso de amido e outros aditivos do arroz, como o pó. Incline cuidadosamente a tigela para escorrer a água, usando as mãos para manter o arroz na tigela. Repita mais 3 vezes. A água nunca será “límpida”, mas será menos turva. Encha novamente o recipiente com água doce e deixe o arroz de molho em água por 10 minutos.
